short_answer: Not for signing something you already have. DocuSign is a service for sending documents to other people and collecting their signatures with an identity trail, and that is what its subscription buys. If a lease, a form or a permission slip has landed in your inbox as a PDF and you just need your signature and a date on it, the free tool here does that in your browser with nothing uploaded.
paywall:
Signing a document someone sends you through DocuSign is free. The paid plans are about sending: after a few free envelopes you pay per month for the right to request signatures from others, with tiers by volume and features.

The confusion is that people search for DocuSign when what they actually need is to put their own signature on a PDF. The free web tools that fill that gap usually cap you at a couple of tasks a day, add a watermark, or require an account, and every one of them uploads your document to do it. Your lease, your ID, your contract, on someone else's server.
free_does:
• Opens the PDF in your browser and renders every page.
  • Draw, type or upload your signature, then place it, move it and resize it. Optionally remember it on your device.
  • Add text boxes, today's date, ticks and crosses anywhere on any page.
  • Downloads a normal signed PDF. No account, no daily limit, no watermark, and the file never leaves your computer.
when_pay:
• You need other people to sign and you need proof of who signed, when, and that the document was not changed afterwards. That audit trail is the product.
  • You send documents for signature regularly and want reminders, templates and tracking.
  • A counterparty or regulator specifically requires a certified electronic signature.
